sources.name: JSON-LD 1.1
sources.role: JSON-based Linked Data serialization, context, term/IRI mapping and graph-expression contract
verified_facts: JSON-LD 1.1 defines a JSON-based syntax for serializing Linked Data.
A context maps terms to IRIs and can control how values and identifiers are interpreted.
JSON-LD processing can expand, compact and otherwise transform a JSON-LD document while preserving its data model.
semantic_limits: Successful JSON-LD parsing or expansion proves serialization conformance, not source authority or real-world truth.
A context mapping can change interpretation and must not substitute for pinned source bytes, version and provenance.
JSON-LD graph expression must not create a parcel-height result without exact HMLR geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and execution receipts.

sources.name: RDF Dataset Canonicalization
sources.role: deterministic RDF dataset canonicalization, blank-node labeling and canonical hash-input contract
verified_facts: RDFC-1.0 defines an algorithm for canonicalizing RDF datasets.
Canonicalization deterministically assigns identifiers to blank nodes and produces a canonical dataset representation.
Canonical forms can support repeatable hashing and change detection for an RDF dataset.
semantic_limits: A deterministic canonical form proves normalization consistency, not that the RDF statements are true or authoritative.
Equal canonical hashes show equality of canonicalized dataset content under the algorithm, not scientific correctness or measurement accuracy.
Canonicalization must not replace source-byte receipts, cadastral authority, geometry completeness, CRS, vertical datum, units or sampling provenance.

sources.name: Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
sources.role: CSVW table/group/column/cell annotation, schema, validation and conversion metadata contract
verified_facts: The specification defines a vocabulary for metadata that annotates tabular data.
Metadata can describe groups of tables, tables, columns and individual cells.
Annotated tables support downstream validation, conversion, display and search.
semantic_limits: CSVW metadata describes how tabular data should be interpreted; it does not prove that the underlying CSV bytes are complete or authoritative.
A successful schema or datatype validation does not prove parcel geometry, height semantics, vertical datum or numeric accuracy.
Cell-level annotation must not become a business row without exact source bytes, authoritative parcel binding and measurement receipts.

sources.name: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.role: dataset, data service, distribution, catalog, version and dataset-series metadata contract
verified_facts: DCAT 3 is an RDF vocabulary for interoperable data catalogs on the Web.
It provides classes and properties for describing datasets, distributions, data services and catalogs.
DCAT 3 adds support for versioning, dataset series and related metadata while preserving compatibility with prior DCAT terms.
semantic_limits: A DCAT dataset or distribution record increases discoverability but does not prove that distribution bytes were fetched, complete or current.
Version and series metadata must be bound to an exact canonical object before any measurement is accepted.
Catalog interoperability must not substitute for exact HMLR polygon, terrain source authority, CRS, vertical datum, units, method, digest and execution receipts.
